headline: Tawfique Nawaz, husband of Dipu Moni, dies at 79
summary: The senior lawyer and Oxbridge-educated advocate of the Supreme Court passed away at a hospital in Dhaka on Tuesday night.
details: Tawfique Nawaz, a senior lawyer and husband of former Awami League minister Dipu Moni, died at Continental Hospital in Dhaka on Tuesday night at 10:27 pm.
An Oxbridge-educated senior advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, Nawaz headed the law firm Juris Counsel and was a member of the Board of Trustees of Transparency International Bangladesh.

He was a member of the Supreme Court Bar Association, the International Law Association, and the Oxbridge Society of Bangladesh, and served as director of the Bangladesh Institute of Law and International Affairs (BILIA) from 1979 to 1982.
Beyond his legal career, Nawaz also practised classical music.
Nawaz had suffered a stroke in 2019, and on May 27 this year, he was brought to court in a wheelchair to meet his wife, Dipu Moni.
Dipu Moni is currently in Munshiganj District Jail as an accused in several cases filed over incidents during the July Uprising.
caption:
Tawfique Nawaz, the husband of former minister Dipu Moni, has passed away at age 79.

He was a member of the Supreme Court Bar Association, the International Law Association, and the Oxbridge Society of Bangladesh, and served as director of the Bangladesh Institute of Law and International Affairs (BILIA) from 1979 to 1982.

Beyond his legal career, Nawaz also practised classical music.

Nawaz had suffered a stroke in 2019, and on May 27 this year, he was brought to court in a wheelchair to meet his wife, Dipu Moni.

Dipu Moni is currently in Munshiganj District Jail as an accused in several cases filed over incidents during the July Uprising.

headline_marked: BRTC launches [[women-only ‘Pink Bus’ service]] with female drivers
headline: BRTC launches women-only ‘Pink Bus’ service with female drivers
summary: 15 women drivers and 24 conductors are now operating 14 buses across Dhaka and other cities to provide safer public transport for women.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has launched a women-only 'Pink Bus' service featuring 15 women drivers and 24 conductors.
A fleet of 14 buses, including both single and double-deckers, will operate on designated routes in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Bogura, and Chattogram.
The service covers 134 stops in total, with 106 located in Dhaka, 12 in Chattogram, and 16 in Bogura.
All staff members have at least HSC-level education, prior driving experience, and valid licenses, having received professional training at the Gazipur training centre.
To enhance safety and convenience, the buses are equipped with Vehicle Tracking Systems, and some currently feature CCTV cameras and Wi-Fi.
An e-ticketing system has been introduced through a partnership with Shohoz.com to reduce waiting times for passengers.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam announced plans to expand the service by adding 100 electric buses, with the first 50 expected within three months.
caption:
Women are now in the driving seat! BRTC launches a dedicated 'Pink Bus' service operated entirely by women.

The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has launched a women-only 'Pink Bus' service featuring 15 women drivers and 24 conductors.

A fleet of 14 buses, including both single and double-deckers, will operate on designated routes in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Bogura, and Chattogram.

The service covers 134 stops in total, with 106 located in Dhaka, 12 in Chattogram, and 16 in Bogura.

All staff members have at least HSC-level education, prior driving experience, and valid licenses, having received professional training at the Gazipur training centre.

To enhance safety and convenience, the buses are equipped with Vehicle Tracking Systems, and some currently feature CCTV cameras and Wi-Fi.

An e-ticketing system has been introduced through a partnership with Shohoz.com to reduce waiting times for passengers.

Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam announced plans to expand the service by adding 100 electric buses, with the first 50 expected within three months.
